channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Board of Trustees taps Vice Chair Mark Chichester as next chair
item.description: GW announced Saturday that the Board of Trustees elected Vice Chair Mark Chichester as its next chair, succeeding longtime leader Grace Speights as the University navigates strategic planning and financial strains.

item.title: GW lifts 10-month freeze on student organization applications
item.description: Officials lifted their yearlong pause on forming new student organizations early, a University spokesperson confirmed, after months of research comparing GW's new organization application and approval process to the University's peer institutions.

item.title: Virginia campus faculty, staff full of questions after GW sidestepped community input on sale
item.description: Faculty and staff operating out of the Virginia Science and Technology Campus said they felt disappointed that officials did not consult them before deciding to sell the campus to Amazon Data Services, though they wish officials’ will engage them in future decision-making.

item.title: Beloved economics professor, principled faculty senator dies at 76
item.description: Colleagues, students and family remember Cordes as a generous, enthusiastic leader who eagerly shared his knowledge of economics with everyone he met.

item.title: Fourth quarter comeback sends women’s basketball to WNIT Super 16
item.description: Women's basketball used a strong fourth quarter to defeat USI and advance to the WNIT's Super 16 on Monday.

item.title: Women’s basketball ends season with 61-53 loss to Illinois State in WNIT Great 8
item.description: Women's basketball ended their season on Monday with a loss to Illinois State University.

item.title: Autry, Benjamin enter transfer portal
item.description: Junior guards Trey Autry and Bubu Benjamin announced they entered the transfer portal on Tuesday.

item.title: Cartoon: Our tuition dollars at work
item.description: Cartoon: Our tuition dollars at work

item.title: Political strategists talk digital media strategy in modern campaigns
item.description: Two political strategists and a GW student campaigner discussed the need for authentic and consistent digital media in campaigns today while addressing the growing use of artificial intelligence in politics.

item.title: Transfer student enters SGA presidential race, advocating for student seat on Board of Trustees
item.description: Alfred Lewis Jr., a first-semester transfer student, is running for SGA president on a platform of "amplifying" student voices and pushing for a voting student member on the Board of Trustees.

item.title: Student Court dismisses SGA presidential candidate’s disqualification appeal
item.description: Zain Masood, a first-year who was convicted of six penalty points for campaign violations, will not appear on the April 16-17 ballot after the Student Court dismissed his appeal for filing past the deadline.

item.title: Academic integrity cases up 47 percent since 2023, CESA reports
item.description: The University reported 103 academic integrity cases in spring 2025, up from 70 in spring 2023, as academic integrity faculty panelist numbers dropped by nearly a third.

item.title: SGA passes resolution backing graduate student union after officials rejected demands
item.description: The Student Government Association unanimously passed a resolution urging the University to bargain more fairly with its graduate student union and guarantee union members will not be overworked.

item.title: How 70 GW students put on the country’s biggest collegiate Bhangra competition
item.description: The thunder of dhol drums and the flash of vibrant costumes will take over Lisner Auditorium this weekend as eight collegiate Bhangra teams battle for Bhangra Blowout's top title.

item.title: GW reaffirms commitment to DEI amid Trump-era pressures, DOJ scrutiny
item.description: Officials upheld GW’s commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion in “every dimension” of the University amid a changing federal legal landscape in a message to community members Thursday.
